intent: The heading that asks an alert dialog's question and gives the popup its accessible name.
typical_uses: The question a confirmation asks, such as "Delete this project?"

dont_use_when.situation: The title of a dismissible modal

invariants.text: AlertDialogTitle renders an h2 with no margin, set at the heading-2 size, line height and tracking with the label weight.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the title's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.states: style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the title's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through alert-dialog.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: A plain heading in place of the title
bad.why: A plain h2 registers with nothing, so the popup gets no `aria-labelledby` and assistive tech announces an alert dialog with no name.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, DialogTitleState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the title's state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property; the primitive passes an empty state object.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: DialogTitleState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function as well as a plain style object; the primitive passes that function an empty state object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`, and the title's state carries no fields. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through alert-dialog.module.css, not through this.
